A seven-point lead and support already at 50% are concrete reasons to move above the crowd price; even all undecided voters moving to Roath would only tie the reported shares if existing preferences held. The poll was commissioned by a Roath-backing PAC, which makes its reported Lynch lead noteworthy, but does not establish the direction of polling bias. Its stated ±4.53-point margin is not the margin of error for the difference between candidates. E2 explicitly calls Lynch the favorite, but Roath's more than $1.1 million raised, reported $25 median donation, and organizational endorsements demonstrate a credible challenge and potential turnout strength. Fundraising and endorsements do not establish a polling lead or sufficient primary turnout. Balancing those concrete signals with substantial uncertainty and the informed crowd estimate, I assign Lynch a 0.64 probability of winning the nomination.
